questions.question: How do you build a JSON API in Rails?
questions.title: Building a JSON API in Rails
questions.direct_answer: A Rails JSON API returns JSON instead of HTML: use rails new --api for a lighter app (no views/assets), render json: in controllers, and set routes with namespace :api. The shape: render json: Post.all (uses to_json), or a serializer for a controlled shape (ActiveModel::Serializers, jsonapi-serializer). Use only: to limit fields and include: for associations to avoid over-exposure. Status codes matter: 201 on create, 204 on destroy, 422 on validation fail. Versioning (namespace :v1) lets you change the API without breaking clients. Keep controllers thin (find, authorize, render json) and put the JSON shape in a serializer once it's complex.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know --api, render json:, status codes, serializers, and versioning (namespace :api/v1) for a JSON API.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Over-exposing the whole model (use only:), or no versioning (breaking clients on change).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: JSON API: --api app, render json:, serializers for the shape, status codes (201/204/422), namespace :v1 for versioning. Keep controllers thin.

sections.title: JSON API Stack
sections.content:
--api + render json: + serializer + status codes + versioning.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[--api: no views] --> R[render json:]
  R --> S[serializer: controlled shape]
  S --> V[namespace :v1: versioning]
  V --> C[201/204/422: status codes]
```

sections.title: A JSON API in Rails
sections.content:
```ruby
# rails new backend --api   (lighter app: no views/assets)

# config/routes.rb
namespace :api do
  namespace :v1 do               # versioning
    resources :posts               # /api/v1/posts
  end
end

# app/controllers/api/v1/posts_controller.rb
module Api
  module V1
    class PostsController < ApplicationController
      def index; render json: Post.all; end

      def create
        post = Post.create!(post_params)
        render json: post, status: :created   # 201
      end

      def destroy
        Post.find(params[:id]).destroy
        head :no_content                    # 204
      end

      private
      def post_params; params.require(:post).permit(:title, :body); end
    end
  end
end

# Complex shape -> a serializer (ActiveModel::Serializers):
class PostSerializer < ActiveModel::Serializer
  attributes :id, :title, :author_name
  def author_name; object.user.name; end
end
# render json: post, serializer: PostSerializer
```
